Since there's no web server, the support chat is probably being exercised through the Genkit Dev UI with the triage or refundAgent, using sessions via `ai.defineAgent` and `.chat()`. Checking `agents.ts`, I notice only refundAgent has a session store — triage and orderAgent don't, which seems like a gap worth investigating.

This matches the bug report: a customer's order status chat can't be resumed by session id. Since triage lacks a `store`, its sessions default to in-memory only, meaning they won't persist across separate requests or a dev server restart — that's likely the root cause of the session-resumption failure.

I want to verify this by checking genkit's actual session/agent code to confirm how the default store behaves and whether it's truly per-call instead of shared.

I need to verify whether defineAgent with no store option defaults to an in-memory store that's shared or per-instance — I should check how defineAgent and agent.chat() handle default storage, especially in the case of orderAgent lacking a store when used within triage via agents().

Let me reconsider: the support chat likely runs through the Dev UI, with sessions tracked via sessionId. It's possible each call to .chat() without an explicit store creates a fresh InMemorySessionStore instance rather than reusing one, which would explain why the session can't be found on a second invocation — the default store isn't cached anywhere. I should search the agent definition code to confirm this.

I found the explicit check that throws an error if you try to resume by snapshotId or sessionId without a store configured — this confirms the root cause: since orderAgent and triage aren't configured with a store, their sessions stay client-managed rather than server-persisted, so they can't be resumed by session id.

This explains why single-turn questions work fine (no resume needed) but follow-ups fail (they require sessionId resumption). The fix is to add `store` to orderAgent and likely triage too, matching what refundAgent already has — I need to figure out which agent is actually the top-level entry point that the frontend calls with sessionId.

Since sub-agents are invoked internally per-delegation and only triage is client-facing, the full conversation state lives in triage's session. So resuming with "What is its status?" requires resuming triage by sessionId, but since triage lacks a `store`, that call would throw a precondition error.

The fix is to add a `store` to triage's agent definition in agents.ts. I should verify the exact precondition error and look at how session resume flows through the agent definition logic.

This confirms the root cause precisely. The `triage` agent — the one the support chat UI actually calls and resumes by session id — has no `store` configured, so it's "client-managed" and resuming it with a `sessionId` throws `AgentInitError: Cannot use 'sessionId' with agent 'triage': this agent has no store configured`. That's exactly "cannot be picked up again by its session id." Single questions still work because a fresh session (no sessionId to resume) never hits this path.

Let me apply the fix: add the shared `store` to `triage`.
